details:
Project Overview

Astro — Mission Commander is an educational browser-based NASA space-outpost simulator.

Players act as commanders responsible for operating either:

  • A lunar base at the Moon’s South Pole
  • A Martian habitat at Jezero Crater

The goal is to make safe mission decisions while balancing:

  • Power
  • Radiation exposure
  • Crew readiness
  • Scientific progress

Main Gameplay

Each mission is divided into 10 sols, or space-mission days.

Every sol:

  1. The simulator generates a solar-weather briefing.
  2. Players review flare severity, radiation risk, and event details.
  3. Players choose an operational decision.
  4. The decision changes power, radiation, and crew resources.
  5. The game advances to the next sol.
  6. The player receives NASA-related science information.

If power, crew readiness, or radiation reaches a dangerous threshold, the mission can fail.

Moon and Mars Modes

Moon Mode

The lunar mission focuses on:

  • Radiation protection
  • Lunar regolith shielding
  • South Pole operations
  • Short Earth-Moon communication delay
  • Lunar temperature extremes

Mars Mode

The Mars mission focuses on:

  • Habitat survival
  • Limited solar energy
  • Long communication delays
  • Mars atmospheric conditions
  • Curiosity RAD radiation measurements
  • Dust and environmental challenges

Moon and Mars have separate visual themes, backgrounds, colors, and mission descriptions.

Chapter 1: Astronaut Training

Chapter 1 contains three interactive stages.

Stage 1 — Discover the Invisible Threat

Players identify radiation sources such as:

  • Solar particle events
  • Galactic cosmic rays
  • Magnetic-field exposure

Incorrect selections display corrective feedback.

Stage 2 — Build Your Shield

Players select protective materials while balancing:

  • Material mass
  • Radiation protection
  • Habitat construction limits

Materials include water, polyethylene, regolith, and habitat wall designs.

Stage 3 — Survive the Solar Storm

Players respond to an approaching solar particle event by selecting safe actions:

  • Move the crew to shelter
  • Pause outdoor activity
  • Save emergency power

Unsafe actions, such as continuing an EVA during the storm, generate warning feedback.

When all three stages are completed, the game displays:

Congratulations! All Chapter 1 stages cleared.

Chapter 2 is then unlocked.

Chapter 2: Historical Solar Storm Lab

Chapter 2 uses the supplied historical dataset:

may_2024_solar_events_starter_dataset.json

This chapter studies the May 2024 Gannon/Mother’s Day solar storm.

The dataset contains:

  • 11 solar flare records
  • 3 solar energetic particle records
  • Observed flare classifications
  • SEP event times
  • Proton energy thresholds
  • Measured proton flux values
  • Event descriptions
  • Source references

Known measured values include:

  • 208 pfu at the ≥10 MeV channel
  • 116 pfu at the ≥10 MeV channel
  • One event where the peak value was not reported

The application deliberately displays missing measurements as “Not reported” instead of inventing values.

NASA Data Usage

The project uses:

  • NASA DONKI space-weather event data
  • NASA CCMC solar-storm information
  • GOES proton-flux measurements
  • Curiosity RAD Mars radiation data
  • NASA mission and environmental references

The existing fallback data is stored in:

nasa_fallback.json

The May 2024 historical data is kept separately so event metadata and measured proton observations are not incorrectly treated as the same type of data.

Technical Structure

Main files:

  • index.html — application layout, chapter selection, overlays, and startup logic
  • src/js/gameState.js — mission state and resource tracking
  • src/js/gameController.js — game loop and decision handling
  • src/js/eventEngine.js — solar-event generation and NASA data fallback logic
  • src/js/ui.js — gameplay panels, stage interactions, Chapter 2 historical lab, and debrief screens
  • src/styles/main.css — responsive visual styling and Moon/Mars themes

Educational Purpose

The project teaches children and new learners about:

  • Space radiation
  • Solar flares
  • Solar energetic particles
  • Habitat shielding
  • Power management
  • Crew safety
  • Scientific data quality
  • Real NASA mission constraints

It combines storytelling, colorful visuals, interactive challenges, and real scientific data into a playable astronaut-training experience.
